title: Random forest predicts three-month outcomes after stroke thrombolysis
summary: Random-forest models predicted three-month functional outcome after intravenous thrombolysis in a retrospective 488-patient stroke cohort, with additional evaluation on two cohorts from another center. Day-seven NIHSS was the most important predictor, so this is a post-treatment prognosis result rather than a tool for choosing initial thrombolysis. Reported performance varied across cohorts; the study does not establish improved treatment decisions or patient outcomes.
ai_technology: Random forest with SHAP, LIME and eli5 explanations
organization: Shanghai Pudong New Area People’s Hospital; Shanghai Eighth People’s Hospital; Fudan University

evidence.tested: 488 patients split 70/30 for training/testing, with 10-fold cross-validation described; internal test mean F1 0.825 for RF versus 0.653 SVM and 0.777 logistic regression. Additional retrospective cohorts contained 316 conventional and 114 wake-up-stroke patients.
evidence.unknown: No prospective decision-impact test or independent replication. Day-seven predictors are unavailable at treatment selection. Text and tables report inconsistent feature counts (16 versus20) and training sample totals (341 versus342); external metrics are source-reported and do not prove universal superiority.
evidence.ai_role: A trained random forest combines clinical variables to predict three-month modified Rankin outcome; explanation methods identify influential features, especially day-seven NIHSS.

source_review.scope: Cached original Frontiers full main text: publication metadata, cohort definition, Methods, model splitting/tuning, Results including external validation, and limitations; supplements not independently read.
